Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Traditional industries and AI: When old meets new 1 day ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Darran Mashall BBC News NI BBC Kukoon Rugs chief executive Paul Vallely says every department in his company uses AI "extensively" Carpet making may be one of the oldest skilled jobs in the world, but even this traditional industry has begun to adopt the most modern of technologies – Artificial Intelligence (AI). Kukoon Rugs is a family-owned firm that sells online and through some of the biggest retail chains in the UK and Ireland. pages.text: Austrian and Swiss women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya 22 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basillioh Rukanga and Makuochi Okafor , BBC Africa Christoph Greztmacher Eva Greztmacher, 76, had spent many years in Niger as an aid worker Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian – have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi. Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year. No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed. The Austrian and Swiss governments have both confirmed the release of their citizens. The Swiss government said Abbt was free and on her way back to Switzerland, while Austria said Gretzmacher had been released after "intensive diplomatic efforts". "We are all very relieved that Eva G. is free again after more than 21 months... For many months, we worked closely, discreetly, and in a spirit of trust with our regional, European, and international partners. pages.text: Aviso sobre la Ley de Ausencia Familiar y Médica | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Aviso sobre la Ley de Ausencia Familiar y Médica El Departamento de Trabajo exige que todo empleador sujeto a la Ley de Ausencia Familiar y Médica exhiba y mantenga exhibido un cartel preparado por el Departamento que resuma las provisiones principales de la Ley de Ausencia Familiar y Médica y que instruya a los empleados en el proceso de presentar querellas/quejas. El cartel se ha de exhibir en un sitio conspicuo donde los empleados y los solicitantes de empleo lo puedan ver. Se tiene que exhibir un cartel en todo sitio de empleo aunque no haya ningún empleado elegible en él. Se pueden procurar ejemplares del cartel preparado por el Departamento (WH 1420SP) para su información o para colgar en el sitio de empleo. Éstos se pueden imprimir a color con un impresor a color o con una versión blanca y negra. Se recomiendan impresores con 1 MB de memoria por lo menos. Para imprimir un ejemplar, favor de seguir estas instrucciones: Se puede disponer de este archivo sólo en el formato PDF. Para ver y/o imprimir documentos en PDF, ha de tener un programa que lea ese tipo de archivo (e.g., Adobe Acrobat Reader® v5 ) y que esté a su alcance en su sitio de trabajo. Pulse en el enlace para el cartel de la Ley de Ausencia Familiar y Médica y espere hasta que salga en pantalla. Para imprimir, pulse sobre el icono (dibujito) que representa el impresor ya adentro del Acrobat Reader. No seleccione la opción de imprimir que aparece en el navegador. Close b-jazz Mapper since: May 07, 2017 Last map edit: November 16, 2026 My Story One of things I like to do when meeting new mappers is ask them how they discovered and started contributing to OSM. Well my story goes back to the very, very early days of OSM. I heard about it through some forums (I don’t even remember which) and took a look at it. To say that the tools were in their infancy would be an understatement. There were no aerial images to make use of, things were mostly done through GPS tracks. Living in the heart of Silicon Valley, there were already some roads mapped out. There were areas right where I lived that were definitely wrong, but the tools just weren’t there for me to invest time, so I walked away for several years. Many years later, I was doing some geocaching in my spare time and there was a big stink when geocaching.com moved from Google maps to OSM. At the time, I didn’t get why they would do that. (A while later it became painfully obvious as I realized that Google was charging through the nose for high traffic users of their services.) I didn’t really pick up OSM at that time either. Add another year or two and I saw that Strava had switched from Google to OSM as well and I really started to be more aware that OSM was becoming more and more mainstream. When I retired in 2017, I wanted to have a project to work on so I started learning OSM and finding more and more ways to contribute. Written 2025-10-30… Published 2026-11-03 About three years ago, during my day-to-day mapping activities, I came across a golf course that had some obvious errors. I didn’t think much of it at the time. Just a fairway that was drawn right across the top of a green. But the more golf courses I looked at, the more frequently I encountered this error. I soon learned about a golf course simulator video game that was built on OpenStreetMap data and was attracting a large influx of simulator enthusiasts who weren’t seasoned OSM mappers. Along with that came various tools to aid in converting OSM data into these simulators, as well as tutorial videos that made some very bad assumptions about how golf courses should be mapped. These factors set the stage for some very bad mapping practices to spread around the world. My understanding is that attempts were made to correct these bad habits at the source, but the tutorial author wasn’t interested in revising or removing his video. Combine that with YouTube’s bad decision to hide down votes on videos, and you’re left with de facto training material that is widely disliked but that new golf course mappers have no way of knowing is a poor source of truth. Secretary of the Treasury Alexander Hamilton stepped forward with a plan to establish a national bank—which still stands in Independence National Historical Park—that would give the federal government more authority to handle the fiscal situation. NPS Comprised of 2.7 million acres on the Seward Peninsula in northwest Alaska, Bering Land Bridge is one of the nation's most remote national park units. Established by the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act (ANILCA) on December 2, 1980, the preserve aims to protect a landscape that contains an invaluable record of flora and fauna, the history of human migration between Asia and North America and supports an ongoing tradition of subsistence culture. An opportunity to travel to a land visited by so few can provide solitude and beauty not often available in others parts of the country. Proper planning and equipment is needed for a successful trip as its remote nature makes it difficult to call for help and can take several hours to reach medical facilities. One night, about two years ago, a group of armed men raided her village. "They scared our cattle away and abducted a girl. We had to run away. We walked barefoot all the way here," she says.
